title: Infinite Elo!!
reviewNotes: Montages, captions and native complete diagrams reviewed. Native54/55 confirm the complete eleven-piece final board after Nxb8+: White Kg1/Nb8/a2/b2/d5/e4/f2 against Kd7/a6/c7/f6, Black to move in check. Every legal answer is a king move: Ke8, Kd8, Kc8, Ke7 or Kd6. The two new Kc8/Nc6 and Kd6/Nc6 comparisons are independently supplied legal continuations, not recovered source moves or exact win claims. The final queen capture gives check but does not itself mate or promote a pawn; all eight pawns remain. Verify all five king replies and the complete larger knight-and-pawn conversion, plus the earlier queen escapes. Previous thirteen-piece rook-offer draft and review history remain preserved; the narrator’s rating metaphor and queen gain are not outcome proof. Full images/captions are available.

So, it seems like the hero is hopeless and he should just give up in this position. But the hero knows that rating is just a number. This is defended. All of these are defended. If he goes here, there's going to be another fork. And so he decides to go to C8. Now he has access to this very long diagonal and this entire row. The rook can still take the knight. The rook is untouchable due to another fork. But since the rook has left the corner now, the queen is able to go back all the way to C8. And it almost seems like the queen is making an escape. White is not giving up and he comes back. Rook to H8. The queen has to go to B7. But now after one last sacrifice, rook to B8. There is simply no place to hide. The entirety of this row is taken by the rook. These squares are defended and so is this one. And in both of these squares, there will be a fork with the knight.
